chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who bought foodstuff from a man with dirhams, so he took half of it and left half of it. Then he came after that and the foodstuff had increased in price or decreased. He (peace be upon him) said: If on the day he bought it, he priced it for such and such, then his price is for him. And if he had only taken some and left some, and did not specify a price, then his price is the price of the day in which he takes it, whatever it was.

key_terms.سَاعَرَهُ: he priced it / he set the price

ai.seo_question: How is the price determined for food bought in bulk but taken in parts if the market price changes?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'sairah' (market rate) in partial delivery sales, distinguishing between fixed-price contracts and open-ended agreements to prevent unjust enrichment from price volatility. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness (adl) and the prevention of gharar (uncertainty) by anchoring value to the time of actual possession rather than arbitrary future dates. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al-buyu' for ensuring that neither party suffers loss due to market fluctuations when the full quantity is not delivered at once.
